Facts A and B were re-executed, not assumed. (A) PRAGMA foreign_keys = OFF inside a transaction is a no-op: it still reported 1. (B) With foreign keys live and movimientos rows referencing reservas, DROP TABLE reservas fails with FOREIGN KEY constraint failed, while the identical statement SUCCEEDS on an empty database. Both reproduced on the sqlite3 CLI 3.53.4 and, decisively, on SQLite 3.51.3 compiled from the exact amalgamation libsqlite3-sys 0.37 bundles for rusqlite 0.39, using that crate's own build flags.

The rebuild order mandated by 00-spec.yaml invariant 4 was executed end to end against a seeded database on SQLite 3.51.3: consumo_por_conversacion returned identical values before and after (conv1=26, conv2=0), zero rows were lost (4 reservas, 7 movimientos), user_version reached 4, PRAGMA foreign_key_check was clean, both indexes were present, every table reported strict=1, no helper table survived, and the recreated movimientos DDL was byte-identical to the original with all six of its constraints still firing.

SQLite DDL is fully transactional here, proved rather than assumed: an explicit ROLLBACK of the rung and an abandoned transaction both left the database at version 3 with id_conversacion still NOT NULL, no consumo_de_ingesta view and no residual helper table. A half-rebuilt accounting table is therefore not a reachable state, and because the runner raises user_version inside the same transaction, schema and version cannot disagree.

The handed claim that a raw rusqlite Connection::open has PRAGMA foreign_keys OFF by default is FALSE in this workspace, and so is the comment at crates/hexcell-storage/src/pools.rs:438. libsqlite3-sys 0.37 build.rs line 126 compiles the bundled amalgamation with -DSQLITE_DEFAULT_FOREIGN_KEYS=1 and rusqlite never turns it off; a driver built from that exact amalgamation reported foreign_keys = 1 with no pragma set. Recorded as risk R-2. The new test still sets the pragma explicitly, for intent and for portability to a system-SQLite build.

The human's declared risk of high stands and is correct. The scorer sees only file count and is blind to the semantics: a naive rebuild here passes the entire test suite green while destroying every existing production cell on upgrade. 00-spec.yaml was not modified.

The human accepted both findings on 27 de agosto de 2026 and amended 00-spec.yaml: invariant 4 now mandates PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys and rebuilding ONLY reservas (movimientos never dropped, copied or recreated; no helper or staging table), and invariant 12 now records the corrected foreign-key default. Blueprint and contract were rewritten to the amended spec. The human also approved blueprint step 8 as a deliberate scope addition.

Executing invariant 4's sequence exactly as written against SQLite 3.51.3 FAILS at COMMIT with FOREIGN KEY constraint failed, even though PRAGMA foreign_key_check reported 0 violations before the commit and all 4 rows had been copied. SQLite's deferred-violation counter is incremental, not a scan: DROP TABLE reservas incremented it and nothing decremented it, because the replacement rows were inserted while the table still bore the name reservas_nueva. The counter and the full scan disagree. Recorded as blueprint risk R-2.

PRAGMA defer_foreign_keys = OFF issued mid-transaction does NOT validate pending deferred violations, it SILENTLY DISCARDS them. Proved by deleting a parent reservas row referenced by two movimientos rows, setting the pragma OFF, and watching COMMIT SUCCEED; the committed database then reported 2 foreign-key violations and 2 orphaned ledger rows. The rung needs that line to commit at all, so the design pairs it with an explicit full-database gate placed immediately before it. Recorded as blueprint risk R-1, the most dangerous line in the task.

A bare PRAGMA foreign_key_check only returns rows and never aborts, and SQLite has no RAISE outside a trigger, so the gate assigns TEXT into the STRICT INTEGER column saldo.disponible on the failing branch only, via CASE. Both paths were executed: the healthy rung committed with saldo unchanged at disponible=934 reservado=40, and a deliberately broken rung (one parent row omitted from the copy) ABORTED with 'cannot store TEXT value in INTEGER column saldo.disponible', leaving the database untouched at version 3 with id_conversacion still NOT NULL and 0 violations. The gate is load-bearing, not decorative.

PRAGMA legacy_alter_table = ON does NOT stop ALTER TABLE from rewriting movimientos' foreign-key reference on SQLite 3.51.3: after renaming reservas aside under that pragma, movimientos' stored DDL had already been rewritten to the new name. Any rebuild that renames the OLD reservas therefore corrupts the ledger's foreign key. Recorded as blueprint risk R-3 so nobody retries it.

The adopted rung was executed against the seeded database on SQLite 3.51.3: movimientos' stored DDL is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after (it is never recreated), zero rows lost (4 reservas, 7 movimientos), consumo_por_conversacion identical (conv1=26, conv2=0), consumo_de_ingesta returns integer 0 not NULL, user_version=4, foreign_key_check clean, 0 non-STRICT tables, id_conversacion nullable, 0 residual tables, 15 schema objects, and defer_foreign_keys auto-reset to 0 with foreign_keys back to 1. A ROLLBACK left the database at version 3 with no residue, the empty-database ladder 0001-0004 ended clean at 15 objects, an ingestion reservation of 50 reconciled at 8 yielded consumo_de_ingesta=42, and all six AC-3 negatives are still rejected.

The stale comment at crates/hexcell-storage/src/pools.rs:438 is NOT fixed here, because pools.rs is outside the touch list and explicitly forbidden. The correction is recorded in three places for a future documentation task: blueprint risk R-8, 00-spec.yaml invariant 12 as amended by the human, and this trace event.

All eight non-cargo guards were re-run against main exactly as written. The only negated guard over pre-existing files, the Spanish lexical one, PASSES (rc=0) with its \b word boundaries intact through the YAML round trip. The guard forbidding DROP TABLE movimientos is negated but scoped to the new file, so it passes vacuously (rc=0), and the foreign_keys=ON check passes on existing test content (rc=0). The five remaining guards are positive existence checks on content this task creates (defer_foreign_keys, pragma_foreign_key_check, the single-occurrence and ordering checks on defer_foreign_keys = OFF, and consumo_de_ingesta in the tests) and are therefore red on main by design.
